projects.title: Chu-nan High School Extension Building
description: Draws inspiration from the colors and character of neighboring buildings. By observing the surrounding architecture, the design takes inspiration from its existing color palette to create a meaningful connection with the local environment.

Rather than copying nearby buildings, the design brings their colors together in a fresh and balanced way. Through the use of different tones, materials, and textures, the building creates a visual harmony while maintaining its own identity.

Beyond its appearance, the concept also represents bringing people together. Just as different colors can form a harmonious whole, the architecture aims to create a welcoming space where people can gather, interact, and feel connected to their surroundings.

projects.title: Ta-kang Junior High School Extension Building
description: The concept, “The Art of Tangram,” draws inspiration from the traditional Chinese puzzle 七巧板, where seven simple geometric pieces come together to form countless shapes and compositions. Similarly, the architecture explores how individual forms can be arranged and combined to create a unified design with its own identity.

Through the arrangement of different geometric volumes, spaces, and functions, the building creates a balance between individuality and unity. Each element maintains its own character while contributing to the overall architectural composition, allowing different forms and spaces to interact in a meaningful way.

Beyond its geometric expression, the concept represents creativity, flexibility, and connection. Just as tangram pieces can be rearranged into different compositions, the architecture seeks to create adaptable spaces that encourage interaction, exploration, and new possibilities.
projects.disclaimer: Disclaimer: All drawings and renderings are for conceptual purposes only. The as built project will differ from the renderings shown in this gallery.

projects.title: Wen-hsin Elementary School 4th Phase Extension Building
projects.brief: When you bring life to the courtyard
description: The concept places the central courtyard at the heart of the campus, creating a close connection between nature, ecology, and learning. By completing the existing U-shaped campus layout, the fourth phase forms a more enclosed and connected space that brings the campus together as a whole.

Rather than serving as an empty space between buildings, the courtyard becomes an active center of campus life. Natural light, wind, water, and greenery are carefully integrated to create a comfortable and sustainable environment where nature can thrive alongside educational activities.

Beyond its environmental benefits, the courtyard encourages students and teachers to gather, interact, and learn beyond the classroom. It becomes a living space that changes with the seasons, supporting biodiversity while creating a healthier and more engaging campus for everyone.

projects.title: Bumi Pakubuwono PIK 2
projects.brief: When you bring mother nature into your home
description: This project is born from a careful analysis of its context—a canal nestled between two prime plots, designated for twin towers. Rooted in the essence of the Bumi Pakubuwono brand, the design focuses on crafting an experience that is luxurious, innovative, and deeply connected to the environment.

The concept centers on integrating nature into the very fabric of the building. The towers are strategically oriented to embrace the canal, offering inclusive views while incorporating lush vegetation that organically grows from the ground floor to the rooftop. Through meticulous zoning, the program ensures optimal space efficiency without compromising on the spectacular vistas that define the project.

The design culminates with a seamless connection between the two towers—a continuous canopy that stretches from one tower to the pedestrian walkways, finally linking to the second tower. This unifying element enhances both the visual appeal and the experience of movement through the site, reinforcing the harmony between architecture and nature.

projects.title: Marketing Gallery PIK 2
projects.brief: An explorative gallery design with thoughts of bringing life to the surrounding
description: This project is an innovative marketing office and gallery designed specifically for the Pantai Indah Kapuk 2 (PIK 2) district. It begins with a creative exploration of nature-inspired forms, drawing from elements such as trees, fungi, and organic structures to craft a building that stands as a vibrant jungle oasis amidst the conventional architectural landscape of surrounding residential complexes.

The program includes a dynamic office space, a central main hall for exhibitions and maquettes, a restaurant, and an expansive outdoor event area. Through a deliberate selection of materials and design elements, this project embodies the very essence of the Pasadena District, serving as the striking first impression of PIK 2, where nature seamlessly intertwines with modern functionality.

projects.title: Re-Unite Bahari
projects.brief: When the Past meets the Present
description: This architectural project serves as the final assignment for the Undergraduate Architecture Program, focusing on the concept of Urban Acupuncture. It investigates the potential for creating significant, transformative spaces through small, deliberate interventions.

At the heart of the design is an exploration of the everydayness of both locals and urban nomads who inhabit the Hexagon Fish Market. Chosen as the site due to its ongoing physical and social decline, the market has become a landscape of abandoned structures and overgrown vegetation, a testament to years of neglect.

Once a thriving hub for commerce and community, this market ceased its traditional operations as it entered the 21st century, now serving as a gathering space for the urban nomads. The project reimagines this space, transforming it into a place that seamlessly integrates the everydayness of the past with the present daily routines of urban nomads, fostering a new sense of place amidst the ruins.

projects.title: Bo.Tani Hub
projects.brief: When the East meets the West
description: This architectural project is driven by the thought-provoking question, “What occurs when the East encounters the West?” It seeks to explore the dynamic intersection of Western technology with the deeply rooted traditions of Indonesia’s agricultural culture.

In response to this question, the design juxtaposes these two realms, each represented as distinct entities. The modern technological aspect of the building is situated on the western section of the site, forming a distinctive zone where advanced technologies—such as UV light radiation, hydroponics, artificial intelligence, and the Internet of Things, etc—can function in harmony.

On the other hand, the traditional aspect of the building is thoughtfully positioned on the eastern side of the site, fostering a space where the farming community and its cultural heritage can flourish. Here, a harmonious coexistence unfolds, as human traditions and practices merge with the advanced non-human agents (NHAs) integrated into the environment. This arrangement cultivates a dynamic yet balanced coexistence, where both human and technological elements contribute to a shared, sustainable future.
